title: Meta and Microsoft pull back from Claude as Anthropic transforms from partner into competitor
source_used: The Decoder (https://the-decoder.com/meta-and-microsoft-pull-back-from-claude-as-anthropic-transforms-from-partner-into-competitor/) and Investing.com on Yahoo Finance, both relaying The Information; The Information's own article is paywalled, its public preview was read.
key_facts: The Information reported on 5 Oct 2026 that Meta and Microsoft, two of Anthropic's biggest corporate customers, are working to cut their employees' use of Claude (The Information's public preview).
At Microsoft, internal Claude spending had been projected at over $1 billion a year; it has been cut by more than a third (The Decoder; Investing.com).
Microsoft executives Scott Guthrie and Jay Parikh told employees to use in-house tools such as GitHub Copilot and OpenAI's models instead (The Decoder).
The reduction applies to internal operations only; customer spending on Anthropic models through Microsoft's enterprise platforms continues to grow (Investing.com).
At Meta, Claude Code users fell from roughly 60,000 to 30,000, partly because of layoffs and partly because Meta is pushing its own tools, Muse Code and MetaCode (The Decoder).

Muse Code, a Claude Code competitor powered by Meta's models, began external testing in August and has over 6,000 internal users; MetaCode, built for internal use, has over 30,000 users (Investing.com).
In one 28-day stretch Meta spent over $105 million on Claude Code alone; Meta had introduced AI cost-cutting measures in June (The Decoder).
quote_evidence: Meta and Microsoft, two of Anthropic's biggest enterprise customers, are sharply cutting internal use of Claude.
At Microsoft, Claude spending had been projected at over $1 billion annually, according to The Information.
Notably, this reduction applies exclusively to internal operations; customer spending on Anthropic models via Microsoft's enterprise platforms continues to see steady growth.
why_it_matters_hint: Two of Anthropic's biggest corporate customers are using less of Claude internally, which The Information calls a challenge for Anthropic's fast growth.
event_date: The Information report of 5 Oct 2026 (18:14 UTC)
notes: The Information's own article is paywalled; its public preview confirms the opening line and the 5 Oct 2026 date. Text read on The Decoder (the pool item) and Investing.com via Yahoo Finance. The Decoder's own commentary (cost savings, Anthropic turning from partner into competitor, Meta wanting to limit Anthropic's data access) is the outlet's view and is not used as fact. Not used: The Decoder's figure of a monthly per-employee budget cut from $100,000 to about $10,000, which looks doubtful and is absent from the Investing.com account.
